title: Spotting Drug Use in Customers
blurb: The signs of drug use, why you never confront or search anyone, and how to report concerns to the Duty Manager.
siteNotes: Who the Duty Manager is on each shift and how to reach them quietly
How often toilets are checked, and who does it
When the venue involves the police (the manager decides)
legalNotes: Licensing Act 2003: the premises licence holder and staff have a duty to promote the licensing objectives, including preventing crime and disorder and protecting public safety. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2003/17

CHECK: the trainer says to refuse alcohol to someone under the influence of drugs. Alcohol must not be sold to a drunk person (Licensing Act 2003, s.141); confirm the venue policy for someone you suspect is on drugs but not drunk.
CHECK: the signs listed (frequent toilet trips, nosebleeds, jitteriness) can have innocent causes, including medical ones. The slides say they are signs to pass to a manager, not proof.
The no-confront, no-search rule and manager-led response are the trainer's; staff have no power to search a guest.

cards.title: Spotting Drug Use in Customers
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- spot common signs of drug use
- respond calmly without confronting anyone
- pass concerns to the Duty Manager and note facts

cards.title: Be aware, not a detective
cards.body: Drug use can happen in any licensed venue. Knowing how to spot it and respond calmly protects our guests and our licence. It is about awareness and safety, not playing detective.

items.title: Tell a manager
items.text: You pass it on, they lead.

cards.title: Signs to watch for
cards.body: These are signs worth knowing. They are a reason to tell a manager, not proof.

cards.title: Signs you might find
cards.body: Look out for what is left behind.

cards.title: Do not confront or search
cards.body: If you suspect drug use, do NOT confront or search the person. It could put you in danger and it is not your job. Quietly inform the Duty Manager and let them decide.

left.title: Do
items: Keep an eye on their welfare

cards.title: Alcohol, welfare and notes
cards.body: Their safety matters even if they have broken the rules. We would usually refuse further alcohol and monitor the situation. Make a note of what you actually saw, as the manager may need to record it or involve the police.

items.title: Refuse alcohol
items.text: If you believe they are under the influence.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Do not confront or search anyone
- Tell the Duty Manager quietly, and let them lead
- Keep an eye on their welfare
- Usually refuse further alcohol
- Note facts, not guesses

cards.q: If you suspect a customer of drug use, you should search them.
cards.why: Never search them. It could put you in danger and it is not your job. Tell the Duty Manager.

cards.q: Which of these could be a sign of drug use?
options: Very frequent toilet trips and agitation
cards.why: Frequent toilet trips, jitteriness, paranoia, aggression, glazed eyes and nosebleeds are all signs to pass on.

cards.q: If you suspect drug use, who should you inform?
cards.why: Quietly inform the Duty Manager and let them decide what to do.

cards.q: You should keep an eye on the welfare of someone you suspect has taken drugs.
cards.why: Their safety matters even if they have broken the rules.

cards.q: If you believe a customer is under the influence of drugs, alcohol service should be…
cards.why: We would usually refuse further alcohol service and monitor the situation.

cards.q: You should confront the customer directly and challenge them.
cards.why: Confronting could put you in danger. Pass your concern to the Duty Manager.

cards.q: When you make a note of what you saw, should it be facts or guesses?
options: A mix of facts and assumptions
Whatever the other staff think happened
cards.why: The manager may need to record it or involve the police, so keep to facts.

cards.q: Powder residue found on a toilet cistern should be…
options: Ignored, as it may be nothing
Tasted to check what it is
cards.why: Powder residue is a sign to report. Do not ignore or deal with it alone.

cards.q: Two of the reasons we take this seriously are guest safety and protecting our licence.
cards.why: Guest safety first, then protecting our licence, with a manager leading the response.

cards.q: Name one physical sign in a person that might suggest drug use.
cards.why: Frequent toilet trips, jitteriness, paranoia, aggression, glazed eyes and nosebleeds may suggest drug use.
